# Point-to-Prompt · Current experience

**Observed current-source behavior, 1 November 2026.** Product basis: `2b398424`, after rebasing onto the `0.72.0` branch at `b871ca1b`. Source capture build: `551bb679` (documentation-only change); inherited package version: `0.70.3`. Browser viewport: **1600 × 1000**.

**Read the provenance on each row.** The real Hyperbase Notebook fails discovery on this source. Feature captures use a disposable, CLI-initialized Notebook containing an unchanged copy of the existing Chrome Overview prototype. Screenshots show the running implementation. No edit task was sent.

Capture service: [current-source prototype](http://127.0.0.1:51890/chrome-overview.prototype). Documentation: real Hyperbase Notebook `nb_dcb6f6b6638b4ea99837656f2fd44fdd`, served by its compatible runtime.

## Live Hyperbase · Discovery blocker

The prototype renders, but the **outer application** reports “A valid manifest-v2 Notebook is required for page mutations” and **0 pages**.

The inner Hyperbase chrome is existing prototype content. It is not the application sidebar. The application therefore cannot resolve an active Site or Prototype, and its Point-to-Prompt entry is absent.

**Source:** current checkout on port 51890. **Notebook:** real Hyperbase.

This source expects a root manifest; real Hyperbase stores it under `backstage/config/`. No metadata migration or product repair was performed.

## Live Hyperbase · Diagnostics

The real diagnostics dialog was opened from the outer application. Its snapshot is preserved alongside the browser error and catalog response.

**Default native launch also failed:** selected Paseo daemon was `0.14.0`; this source requires `0.13.2`. The native build passed, but Core startup exhausted recovery.

Current-source browser capture uses the supported private Paseo mode, isolated application state, and an ephemeral proxy port. The shared instance was not repaired or replaced.

**Observed, not inferred:** native lifecycle opening `68936a…`, plus the actual current-source browser screenshot.

## Live Hyperbase · Entry is unavailable

Searching the real command palette for **Point to Prompt** does not provide a usable feature entry in this invalid catalog state.

This is the end of the reachable live-Hyperbase flow on the current source. Later rows are explicitly labeled **capture fixture**.

The documentation itself is saved in real Hyperbase through its compatible running service. No existing canvas is reused or overwritten.

## Capture fixture · Entry

A valid Notebook makes **⌖ Point to Prompt** appear in the application’s prototype header. The copied Chrome Overview renders inside the same-origin iframe.

**Provenance:** supported CLI init; Notebook ID `point-prompt-capture-fixture`; `/private/tmp/point-prompt-capture-2gzj7j08`; unchanged source copied from real Hyperbase’s `prototypes/chrome-overview.prototype`. Existing dependencies are linked; none installed.

This is the current running implementation, with real prototype content. It is not proof that live Hyperbase discovery works.

## Capture fixture · Empty panel and terminal

Clicking the entry opens the right panel. It identifies **Chrome Overview** and `/chrome-overview.prototype`, then offers **Inspect element**, **Region**, an instruction field, **Add to batch**, and **Send**. Empty instructions disable both actions.

The terminal is visible, but reports **startup context has not been acknowledged**. Its real Copilot output presents folder trust. No trust confirmation or terminal input was entered.

The terminal heading overlaps the widget chrome in this viewport. Capture records that state; no UI repair was made.

## Capture fixture · Inspect an element

Click **Inspect element**, then hover the “Explore page details” link. The real inspector draws a highlight over the target.

The inspected content lives inside the prototype iframe. Selection is mapped back into application coordinates. Clicking in inspection mode captures the element instead of following its link.

This capture exercises same-origin element inspection. Cross-origin Sites and text-range selection were not exercised.

## Capture fixture · Selection plus instruction

Clicking the target adds its DOM selector to the composer. The instruction can then be entered independently.

The sample says: “Capture example only: make the Explore page details link easier to find.” **Add to batch** and **Send** become available.

API readback later confirms element kind, anchor tag, selector, HTML, text, and rectangle. The selected anchor is still on the page.

The visible terminal readiness warning remains. Button availability alone does not prove dispatch readiness.

## Capture fixture · Attach a live screenshot

**Attach live screenshot** successfully captures the selected link and adds a thumbnail. The selection and screenshot have independent remove controls.

This uses the application’s real capture path, not an uploaded mock. The private queue readback identifies a persisted PNG attachment.

The thumbnail is small because the selected element is a short link. The terminal still shows its actual trust/startup state.

Pasting an external clipboard image was not exercised.

## Capture fixture · Queue without dispatch

**Add to batch** creates **Batch · 1** and clears the composer. The item shows its instruction and a remove control; **Send all** is visible.

Readback confirms status `queued`, `kind: prototype`, route, iframe URL, fixture `sourceRoot`, selected DOM, and private screenshot ID. Context remains attached even though the queue row only displays text.

Neither **Send**, **Send all**, nor the keyboard send shortcut was used. Dispatch and editing remain unverified.

After capture, the sample item was removed; readback confirms an empty queue.

## Capture fixture · Select a region

Click **Region**, then drag over the prototype. The composer shows **Selected region** and a real cropped image containing the dragged content.

This draft has no instruction, so Add to batch and Send are disabled. The earlier queued example remains visible during this capture.

The region, screenshot, and queued sample were removed after documentation capture. The capture-only terminal was stopped. The current-source Core service remains available.

This verifies region capture, not a region editing task.

# What this capture establishes

**Working on the supported fixture:** prototype entry, panel/composer, same-origin inspection, selected DOM, live element attachment, persisted queued context, and region attachment. The sample queued prompt was removed; no edit dispatch occurred. The capture-only terminal was stopped.

**Blocking the live Hyperbase flow:** this source does not discover the backstage manifest. Default native startup also rejects the host Paseo version. The documentation canvas is authored through Hyperbase’s compatible service. These setup differences are explicit; the fixture does not establish live-Hyperbase compatibility.

**Not exercised:** Send / Send all / keyboard dispatch, actual coding edits, clipboard paste, cross-origin Sites, or text-range selection. Terminal output and its readiness warning were observed, not repaired. Human acceptance remains pending.

**Evidence:** materialized canvas/widget IDs, screenshot dimensions and hashes, fixture file hashes, queue API readback, native lifecycle evidence, and command results are returned with Lanes Task `#g209#t01`. Capture screenshots are 1600 px wide; live Hyperbase captures are 1000 px high and fixture captures 913 px high.

# Point-to-Prompt · Current experience

Capture build: `551bb679` (documentation-only change); inherited package version: `0.70.3`. Screenshots retain their real dimensions: 1600 × 1000 for live Hyperbase, 1600 × 913 for the fixture.

**Read the provenance on each row.** Real Hyperbase fails discovery on this source. Feature captures use a disposable, CLI-initialized Notebook containing an unchanged copy of the existing Chrome Overview prototype. Screenshots show the running implementation. No edit task was sent.

Capture service: [current-source prototype](http://127.0.0.1:51890/chrome-overview.prototype). Destination: real Hyperbase Notebook `nb_dcb6f6b6638b4ea99837656f2fd44fdd`, served by its compatible runtime.
